_description: CAREER arm E 'ontfull_abs': faithful reproduction of the April 2026 results_v7_lc_*_ontology arm. Identical to lc_career_ontfull.json except ontology_negative_rank_tiers=false, matching April, when that flag did not yet exist (added 2026-07-23 in e89011d, three months after those runs).
_note_on_the_matcher: With ontology_guided_negatives=false AND ontology_weight=0.0, BatchProcessor builds no skill matcher at all (it is gated on 'use_ontology or force_skill_negatives'). So this arm loads no ESCO graph and has no ontology signal anywhere — the esco_* paths below are inert and kept only so the two configs differ in as few lines as possible.
_comment_cache: Dedicated path, shared by BOTH career learning-curve arms. Text embeddings come from the FROZEN encoder, so they are identical across arms and the second arm reuses them for free; nothing arm-specific or learned is cached. It must not be the historical shared 'embedding_cache/text_embeddings.pt': that file predates v7, covers 0% of these content hashes, and writing v7 vectors back into it would grow a file other experiments depend on. Size is set well above the ~16k unique resume/job texts in frac_100 + validation so nothing is evicted; at 10000 the tail of frac_100 thrashes and the hit rate collapses.
_comment_the_factor: THE ONE THING THAT VARIES, here switched OFF.
_comment_skill_distances: Matched to the ontology arm so it cannot become a second factor. Inert here: this arm builds no skill matcher, so nothing reads it.
_why: lc_career_ontfull was NOT a faithful reproduction: it enabled rank tiers, which changes what 'hard negative' means. Measured on frac_20 over 12,000 pairs, the ABSOLUTE hard bucket (d<=0.3) is empty for 60/60 anchors -- the realized minimum distance is 0.3938 -- and medium (0.3-0.6) holds only 1.68% of pairs while easy (>0.6) holds 98.32%. So under April's absolute tiering the ontology delivered no hard and almost no medium negatives, making its negative selection nearly equivalent to random sampling. This arm reproduces that behaviour so the April +0.0226 can be tested directly.
_note_pathway: use_pathway_negatives is included for fidelity to the old arm, but note it is NOT a distinct mechanism: BatchProcessor builds self.career_graph when it is set, yet _select_negatives never consults it — after the gate, control goes to _select_ontology_negatives (the skill matcher) or to random. So pathway and ontology_guided_negatives open the same gate and run the same selection code.
_expected: If +0.0226 was unseeded run-to-run variation, this arm should land near the other three (pooled +0.005 or below, p>0.05). If it lands near +0.02, then something about absolute tiering -- most likely the near-random negatives interacting with ontology sample weighting -- mattered, and the rank-tier 'fix' removed a real effect.
_note_gate: ontology_guided_negatives is false, matching April (the field was absent there). The gate in _select_negatives opens on 'use_pathway_negatives OR ontology_guided_negatives', and use_pathway_negatives is true, so ontology selection still runs -- exactly as it did in April.
_note_scheduler: negative_scheduler is 'fixed' where April had null. Behaviourally identical: with negative_curriculum=false, April's null scheduler falls through _compute_negative_ratios to the unknown-scheduler default (0.33, 0.34, 0.33), which is what 'fixed' with these ratios also returns.
